Conversations within Defence and Peace Economics

1997–2026 catalogue coverage · run 20261015T195408Z-068616ae

1,214 catalogue records; 1,136 eligible papers; 3,080 observed directed links; 3,076 DOI-only links; 189 papers with no observed internal links.

Method

Adapted from Delahais and Thyrard, Conversations in Evaluation and its public replication script. RePEc supplies the article universe; Crossref supplies references. No Scopus data are used.

One node per RePEc handle; one edge from citing to cited paper. Repeated references are deduplicated and article self-loops removed. Shared authors do not remove an edge. Editorials, issue introductions, administrative records, corrections and routine book notices are excluded. Substantive reviews remain eligible. Every decision is preserved in evidence.json.

DOIs are normalized and identities checked against metadata. Unique exact bibliographic matches use journal, volume, first page and author surname, or exact title and surname. Ambiguities require documented review; fuzzy matches are not automatically accepted. The recovered graph is accompanied by a DOI-only baseline. Recovered links and DOI corrections are audited before publication.

Louvain communities are computed on an undirected projection, summing reciprocal edge weights. Resolution 1; seeds 0–19; maximum modularity with deterministic tie-breaking. Selected seed 18, modularity 0.6462. Resolutions 0.5 and 1.5 are sensitivity checks. NetworkX 3.6.1. ForceAtlas2 seed 42, 500 iterations within each component; disconnected components are packed at the right and isolated papers below. Their relative placement is arbitrary. All discovered communities are retained.

Limits and denominators

Pre-1997 papers are outside this catalogue. Publication years follow RePEc issue years, which can differ from first-online dates. 2026 and end periods reflect catalogue availability. Missing Crossref deposits and unmatched references can remove genuine edges; no observed link does not establish no citation. Citations do not establish agreement or substantive intellectual exchange. Community labels describe reviewed leading titles and available abstracts.

Temporal shares use all eligible papers in a period, including papers without observed links; pooled communities remain fixed. Topic comparisons use all eligible community members, with missing and unassigned abstracts reported separately. The bound topic run is 20261015T193744Z-b7bf447b.

Network

Communities

  1. Military spending and economic growth (141 articles): Growth-model specification and heterogeneous economic effects of military expenditure.
  2. Terrorism, counterterrorism and economic costs (132 articles): Terrorist recruitment, deterrence and political policies, and economic costs of terrorism.
  3. Defence industries, innovation and European cooperation (129 articles): European defence policy, industrial collaboration, contractor performance and defence innovation.
  4. Defence spending, alliances and arms races (127 articles): Demand for military expenditure, alliance burden sharing and strategic rivalry, including Greece and Turkey.
  5. Defence budgets, equipment costs and force planning (77 articles): Country surveys and defence budgeting connect to equipment costs, inflation and replacement decisions.
  6. Geopolitical risk, sanctions and financial markets (58 articles): This mixed community connects geopolitical risk and market responses with sanctions and political regimes.
  7. Arms trade, military technology and arms races (55 articles): Strategic arms trade and procurement, defence R&D and equipment quality, and asymmetric arms races.
  8. Military spending and public debt (36 articles): Military spending and external or government debt, with panel and country studies.
  9. Military recruitment, retention and conscription (35 articles): Recruitment incentives, retention, deployment and the choice of military service systems.
  10. Civil war and the economic costs of conflict (35 articles): Civil-war determinants, economic losses and regional spillovers of armed conflict.
  11. Military spending, welfare and inequality (33 articles): Military expenditure, social spending, income inequality and employment.
  12. Third-party intervention and conflict bargaining (30 articles): Leading papers use strategic conflict models to examine intervention, rebellion, territorial disputes and bargaining.
  13. Risk, insurance and emergency provision (4 articles): Leading papers model supply interruptions, risk aversion, insurance and international public goods.
  14. Conflict exposure, education and economic growth (4 articles): This small group connects schooling, child labour and gender differences in education with a study of violence and economic growth in Colombia.
  15. Armoured vehicles and casualty cost-effectiveness (4 articles): This small group includes an explicit published exchange over the data and methods used to evaluate armoured tactical vehicles, together with a linked casualty-care study.
  16. Terrorism research and prevention methods (3 articles): This small group links a taxonomy of terrorism research, a study of predictability before 9/11 and evaluation of camera surveillance. The links alone do not establish one sustained debate.
  17. Illicit small arms and ammunition markets (3 articles): Leading papers trace illicit small-arms supply chains, ammunition diversion and market prices.
  18. Civil-conflict motives and economic shocks (3 articles): This small group connects greed/grievance arguments, economic shocks and institutional accounts of conflict.
  19. Deployment selection, health and education (3 articles): This small group connects selection into deployment with mental health and educational outcomes of deployment and combat.
  20. French First World War military casualties (3 articles): Leading papers use French historical soldier records to study deaths and military executions.
  21. Israeli–Palestinian bargaining and proxy conflict (3 articles): Leading papers model monopolization of violence, proxy-war relationships and obstacles to negotiated resolution.
  22. Militant groups, rivalry and targeting (3 articles): Leading papers connect militant-group ethnicity and rivalry with rebel decisions to target Americans.
  23. Military organization and battlefield performance (2 articles): Two linked papers examine battlefield success and the effects of military unionization. This small pair is a connection rather than evidence of a broad community.
  24. Narcotics, crime and security policy (2 articles): Two linked papers model narcotics restrictions and connect international crime with European threat perceptions.
  25. Civil-war termination and political outcomes (2 articles): Two linked papers study how civil wars end and the political consequences of different outcomes.
  26. Iraq mortality-survey controversy (2 articles): Two linked articles scrutinize the methods, integrity and corroboration of the second Lancet Iraq mortality survey. This label describes the papers’ subjects without adjudicating their claims.
  27. Economic growth and interstate war (2 articles): Two linked papers examine whether economic growth increases the likelihood of interstate conflict.
  28. Swedish military service and later earnings (2 articles): Two linked studies estimate civilian earnings effects of military training and peacekeeping deployment in Sweden.
  29. Nuclear deterrence and defensive weapons (2 articles): Two linked game-theoretic papers examine nuclear acquisition, deterrence and the consequences of asymmetric defensive shields.
  30. Armed violence and economic development (2 articles): Two linked papers address resource dependence, sustainability and the effects of civil war on financial development.
  31. Corruption and procurement accountability (2 articles): Two linked papers model corruption controls and the costs and benefits of procurement bid protests.
  32. Espionage and innovation contests (2 articles): Two linked theoretical papers study economic espionage, copying and competition over innovative effort.
  33. Orbital debris and space security (2 articles): Two linked papers examine space debris, behavioural incentives and the consequences of anti-satellite weapons.
  34. House raids, demolitions and conflict behaviour (2 articles): Two linked studies examine household exposure to state coercion and claims about punitive demolitions and suicide bombing. The label does not establish agreement between them.
  35. Commodity shocks, conflict and peacekeeping (2 articles): Two linked empirical papers examine commodity-price shocks, conflict intensity and the possible buffering role of UN peacekeeping.
